prompt.context: Your client is CNB Movies, a national movie theater company with $2 billion in annual revenue. In recent years, movie theaters have seen record high demand for Marvel and DC Comics movies, and CNB is considering ways to capitalize on this demand. One option is to offer 24-hour opening weekend screenings for these movies. The company has hired you to advise on the decision.
prompt.question: Should CNB Movies offer 24-hour opening weekend screenings for Marvel and DC Comics movies?

clarifying_info.q: When does CNB want to implement this?
What counts as an opening weekend?
clarifying_info.a: Opening weekend starts Thursday night and ends Sunday at 11:59 PM — 3 nights total.

clarifying_info.q: Is this a full rollout or a pilot?
clarifying_info.a: CNB wants to test one theater first. If successful, the company would roll out to all 400 theaters in the US.
$15 for adults; $10 for children and seniors.
None of CNB's competitors currently offer this experience.

clarifying_info.q: Does CNB have the capital to fund this?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, CNB Movies is capable of financing this on its own.

exhibits.title: Expected Seat Utilization Per Showing
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing the percentage of seats filled by audience segment (Children, Adults, Seniors) across three overnight showtimes: 12:00 AM, 3:00 AM, and 6:00 AM. Each bar is segmented by audience type.

exhibits.title: Daily Cost Structure Per Theater (Current Costs)
exhibits.shows: A table listing the current daily cost categories for one theater: Staff, Concessions, Concession Maintenance, and Projector Maintenance, with dollar amounts for each.

data.note: Staff includes cashiers, ticket collectors, film operators, maintenance/cleaning, and security

framework: Revenue: ticket sales (Adults @ $15, Children/Seniors @ $10) across all three overnight showtimes; concessions revenue per attendee
Costs: incremental staff costs (cashiers, ticket checkers, cleaning, extra security); concession COGS; concession machine maintenance; projector maintenance; utilities
Profitability: compare incremental revenue vs. incremental costs to determine net profit per theater per opening weekend

Strategic / qualitative factors: competitive advantage (first mover), risk of projector running 24 hrs, opportunity cost of capital, potential for premium pricing, rollout feasibility across 400 theaters

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, calculate total ticket revenue for one theater across the three overnight showtimes for a single night.
questions.guidance: Candidate should apply the ticket price formula per showtime, accounting for audience mix and 300 seats. Strong candidates compute each showtime separately then sum.

math.setup: Ticket Rev per showtime = 300 seats × [(% children × $10) + (% adults × $15) + (% seniors × $10)]

questions.prompt: Calculate concessions revenue for one theater for a single night. (Average concession spend is $10 per person; provide this only if the candidate asks about other revenue sources.)
questions.guidance: Candidate must notice concessions as a second revenue stream. Calculate total attendees per showtime (300×utilization rate) and multiply by $10.

math.setup: Concession Rev per night = $10 × total attendees across all three showtimes

questions.prompt: Calculate total revenue per theater for the full opening weekend (3 nights).
questions.guidance: Candidate sums ticket and concession revenue per night, then multiplies by 3.

math.setup: Total Revenue = (Ticket Rev + Concession Rev) per night × 3 nights

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2 and the cost increase assumptions below, calculate total costs per theater for the opening weekend. Under the 24-hour model: Staff costs increase 50%; Concession costs increase 50%; Concession maintenance costs increase 25%; Projector maintenance costs increase 10%.
questions.guidance: Candidate must apply percentage increases to each cost line, sum to get new daily total, then multiply by 3 nights.

math.setup: New daily cost per line = current cost × (1 + % increase); Total weekend cost = new daily total × 3

questions.prompt: What is the incremental profit from the 24-hour model for one theater for an opening weekend? What is the profit margin?
questions.guidance: Candidate subtracts total costs from total revenues and computes margin relative to revenue.

math.setup: Incremental Profit = Total Revenue − Total Costs; Margin = Profit / Revenue

brainstorming.prompt: What are some additional factors that CNB should consider before making their final decision on rolling out the 24-hour model?

categories.name: Customer & Demand
ideas: Risk of cannibalizing existing customer base (customers who shift from regular screenings to overnight ones)
Demographic analysis by region — overnight demand may vary significantly by market
Fluctuations in concession sales at late-night showtimes (lower spending at 3 AM vs. midnight)

categories.name: Marketing & Brand
ideas: Upfront marketing costs to promote the new experience
Long-term marketing benefits: word of mouth, press coverage, incremental market share
Whether the experience justifies a ticket price premium over standard $15/$10 pricing

categories.name: Operations & Rollout
ideas: Whether to roll out to all 400 theaters or a targeted subset based on demand
Criteria for selecting which movies qualify (e.g., only proven blockbusters)
Operational complexity: managing staff overnight, food safety for concessions, safety/security concerns

categories.name: Competitive & Strategic
ideas: Competitive response: if CNB does not do this, do competitors capture those customers first?
Whether this sets a precedent for other genres beyond Marvel/DC

categories.name: Financial & Risk
ideas: Projector wear-and-tear from continuous 24-hour operation — capital expenditure implications
Demand and cost assumptions may need further validation before full rollout
Sensitivity analysis on attendance at 3 AM and 6 AM showtimes — utilization could be optimistic

recommendation: CNB Movies should implement the 24-hour opening weekend experience. The expected incremental profit is $10,800 per theater per opening weekend, representing a ~22% profit margin.
If rolled out to all 400 theaters, total incremental profit potential is $10,800 × 400 = $4.32 million per major blockbuster opening weekend.
Offering this experience also provides a first-mover competitive advantage for high-grossing Marvel and DC films.
risks: CNB's demand assumptions (especially for 3 AM and 6 AM showtimes) may be optimistic and require further validation
Projections may vary significantly by theater and geography
Movies could underperform at the box office, reducing attendance and eliminating the profit case
Continuous 24-hour projector operation may increase capital maintenance beyond the assumed 10% increment
next_steps: Develop a marketing strategy to promote the 24-hour experience before the pilot
Conduct sensitivity analysis on attendance and cost assumptions
Determine optimal rollout strategy across the US — prioritize high-demand markets
Establish criteria for which movies qualify for the 24-hour model
Evaluate potential for premium ticket pricing for overnight showtimes
